Messages.Author: Tammy, Chris, and Alex Shorb
Messages.Body:
I have found that my decks tend to be on the slow side, for whatever
reason. While I have tried to make them somewhat faster, I was
wondering what strategies people found worked well to slow down a
game. I have heard mentioned Millicent Smith, which sounds like a
good one. And I have seen things like Autarkis Persecution and
Ancient Influence/Political Struggle slow things down. Others?

Chris

> wondering what strategies people found worked well to slow down a

Why work to slow down the game rather than speed it up?

> I have heard mentioned Millicent Smith, which sounds like a
> good one.

Wanna really slow down a game? pass a Reversal of Fortune first.
While you're at it, pass a First Tradition: Masquerade too.

> And I have seen things like Autarkis Persecution and
> Ancient Influence/Political Struggle slow things down.

Uh...you mean Politcal Stranglehold, don't you?

Autarkis Persecution really rewards weenie decks which are usually
faster, so that's not a good idiea. Ancient Influence/Stranglehold are
okay but they can only be used once each. Using the Fifth Traditional
Hopsital/Minion Tap combo works by giving you more pool.

However, lots of pool gain won't help you if your predator has a rush
combat deck, a political deck that banishes/burns vampires or a
Corruption/Temptation/Mind Rape deck. At one point, A few of us were
working on a deck that made you discard your entire deck.

You're better served by speeding up your game than trying to compensate
for a slow one. I do realize that some really neat deck concepts take a
while to set up...but you don't get to see it work well if your predator
is bleeding you for 3+ at a time with a bunch of Presence weenies.

Messages.Author: c34m...@my-deja.com
Messages.Body:
In article <38CD3868...@alumni.williams.edu>,

shr...@alumni.williams.edu wrote:
> I have found that my decks tend to be on the slow side, for whatever
> reason.

In an average game, you get 2-3 transfers on you first turn and 4 on
each subsequent turn. Although Information Highway, Tomb of Ramsis III
and other cards can improve this, their reliability is negligible
(unless you can put 5 tombs in your library). Therefore, by turn 3 you
can influence ~10 capacity. For a normal deck, this is 1-2 minions,
for weenies, this is 4 minions. Obviously your larger vamps are going
to put you at a significant disadvantage against a weenie deck. Fast
decks are going to be weenier decks so Anarchist Uprising and other
vote cards will help hurt a weenie predator. Also, avoid equipping
larger minions. They usually have sufficient skills to hold their own
and equipping represents another turn without acting directly against
predator or prey. Also, consider a mixture of smaller and larger
minions. I find this works well because the smaller minions can come
out quickly, defend and then do the biding of larger minions. Routers
Hands, Precognizant Mobility, Force of Will and other untapping cards
are also useful for giving you extra actions to get your deck going.
Finally, you can use the table against fast decks. Usually the
strongest player is targeted early in the game because everyone wants
to get his or her deck “up and running”. Therefore, if you are on the
wrong end of a weenie deck, consider working the table in order to get
some help. Weenie decks are a fact of the game, but your methods for
combating them are varied and will usually gain the support of the
majority of the table.

Yep, that's what the ??? was for.

End of turn -> Millicent Moves -> Option to have turn. -> Pay pool ->
Have turn. -> Repeat.

End of turn -> Millicent Moves -> Option to have turn. -> Pass ->
Millicent stuck even with play going to right. (person did not have turn
and thus no end of turn phase to move millicent to next "Option" player.)
